granicus.name: Granicus
granicus.description:
Granicus sells cloud software and services that governments use to communicate with the public, publish and stream meetings, run websites and forms, and manage records and permits. Its own site frames the offering as two platforms: the Government Experience Cloud (GXC), split into Service Cloud ("Deliver services without friction"), Engagement Cloud ("Grow and activate audiences") and Operations Cloud ("Automate workflows and reduce costs"), and the Destination Experience Cloud (DXC) for destination marketing. Layered on those are Government Experience Agent (GXA), described as an AI-powered digital agent built for government, a Federal Experience Cloud, and the GXI Enterprise and GXI Foundations intelligence tiers. The solution pages group the underlying products into agenda and meeting management, websites and CMS, digital services and forms, digital communication and engagement, permitting and licensing, and public records and short-term-rental compliance. The product directory names each tool with its legacy brand in parentheses: Communications (govDelivery), Websites & CMS (govAccess, OpenCities, Intranet), Records Request Management (GovQA and GovQA Legal), Short-Term Rentals (Host Compliance), Forms & Workflow (OpenForms), Service Request Management (govService and OneView), Permitting, Compliance & Licensing (AMANDA and SmartGov), Land & Official Records (govRecords), Sentiment & Feedback (EngagementHQ), Video (self-managed, and Swagit partially and fully managed), Boards and Commissions, and agenda management under the Legistar, OneMeeting and Peak names. The buyers named under "Who we serve" are local government, state government, federal government, education, special districts, elected officials and destinations, with country sites for Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia & New Zealand, India, and Latin America & the Caribbean. Granicus also sells consulting and digital agency work through the Granicus Experience Group (GXG).

Granicus is the parent of this family rather than a member of one. Its company page states "more than 2,000 employees across the globe supporting more than 7,000 public sector organizations," and the careers page repeats "about 2,000 of us" spread across "eight countries" in a remote-first workplace; that page's "Explore roles" button points at careers-granicus.icims.com, the iCIMS board the Simpleview careers page also lands on. The homepage figure block claims 7,000+ public sector customers, 360M people in the Granicus subscriber network, 100% of U.S. federal cabinet-level agencies, 48 of the 50 largest U.S. cities, 30B digital experiences and 22B government messages delivered annually, 8B government website views, 3.5M online forms submitted, 2M record requests served and 123K government meetings streamed each year. The company page carries a timeline headed "Organic and inorganic growth through best-in-class acquisitions": Granicus and GovDelivery were independently founded in 1999 and merged in 2017; Vision Internet arrived in 2018; a London-based government service provider in 2019; Bang the Table, OpenCities and GovQA in 2021 alongside Australia/New Zealand expansion; a full-service video provider and a government CRM in 2022 with entry into Latin America and the Caribbean; Simpleview in 2024; and GXA's launch in 2025. The same page names Vista Equity Partners as an existing investor joined by Harvest Partners in 2020. The trust-center office list gives Denver, Washington DC, Tucson, Ottawa, London, Melbourne, Auckland, San Juan and Bengaluru.

simpleview.name: Simpleview
simpleview.description:
Simpleview sells destination-marketing technology and marketing services to the organizations that promote places. Its own homepage now carries the title "Granicus Destinations | Marketing Solutions | CVB Tourism Software" and the line "From small towns to big countries, Granicus Destinations is the tourism software partner to help you engage stakeholders, attract visitors, and win bids for conventions and events." The product menu lists Simpleview CMS, "designed by and for DMOs"; Simpleview CRM, an industry-specific CRM with "seamless integration with more than 20 programs"; Simpleview DAM for digital assets; Destination Canvas; an Online Booking & Referral Engine branded Book > Direct that "lets visitors book directly with your partners and stakeholders"; Partner Engagement & Website Monetization (DTN), which "facilitates targeted advertising on destination websites" so DMOs can earn revenue; user-generated content; mobile apps; digital accessibility; email marketing and automation via Act-On; digital proposals; event management; short-term rental solutions; and a data tier of Simpleview Data Engine, dashboards, pace reporting and a meetings and groups database. Alongside the software it sells agency work: website design, visual identity, SEO, paid media, digital strategy, a Digital Maturity Model, DMO partner engagement, the Digital Influence Report and training. The acquisition release describes the buyers as "convention bureaus, venues, tourism boards, destination marketing organizations, and attractions." Granicus's destinations page states that "more than 500 DMOs use our CMS," that "1,000-plus destinations" use the CRM, and that 400M+ people visit those websites annually.

Both sites confirm Simpleview is part of Granicus, so the careers redirect is corroborated rather than relied on. Granicus's destinations FAQ asks "Is Simpleview now part of Granicus?" and answers "Yes. Simpleview was acquired by Granicus, and the legacy Simpleview products, services, expertise, and thought leadership are now a part of the Granicus portfolio serving destination marketers," then explains the two-site split: the solutions "remain at simpleviewinc.com" during a transition and "The two websites will be combined in the near future." Granicus's own office list gives Tucson, AZ, 8950 N. Oracle Road as "Simpleview, now part of Granicus" - the address in Simpleview's footer. Simpleview's Our Story page says plainly "We were acquired by Granicus." The Granicus press release of September 5, 2024 announced the acquisition, said Simpleview "works with more than 1,000 premier destinations," quoted Simpleview CEO Ryan George, and put the combined company at more than 7,000 organizations and roughly 2,000 employees. A May 5, 2026 release then announced Granicus Destinations as "a dedicated business segment" with its own leadership and the DXC platform, "supporting more than 1,000 destinations worldwide, including all 11 FIFA World Cup host cities." Our Story dates the business to 2001 as 220 Solutions, founded by Ryan George, Bill Simpson and Scott Wood; the first web-based CRM built for DMOs in 2002, with Visit Lauderdale as first client; a 2007 merger with cvbTV at 100 clients; New Media Gateway in 2010; Software Management, Inc. in 2014, adding 92 DMOs; and later 2Synergize, Jackrabbit Systems, Eventsforce and the MINT+ meetings database.
